current_episode.title: Your Framework is there, It's Just STILL Hidden

guest.bio_context: Amanda Walker has been coaching since age 15 as a competitive athlete, coached basketball and track at high school level, was a science teacher, taught group fitness including step aerobics, spin, and CrossFit for over 10 years, and is the mother of two. She has been part of multiple shifts in the coaching industry over the last 10 years and now specializes in helping coaches discover and articulate their hidden frameworks to build profitable, scalable coaching businesses.

pending_qa.q: Why is building a framework essential for coaches who want to scale beyond six figures?
pending_qa.r: If a coach is serving 20 clients in a caseload and tries to start from scratch with each client while maintaining customization and deliverables, they become exhausted and burnt out. Without a framework, there is such diversity of results coming from the client base that the coach never solidifies what they are known for, making it hard to sell because they cannot clearly articulate the result they provide. A framework is not a should—it is a must for scaling beyond six figures, because it allows the coach to serve more clients without tanking and provides consistent, marketable results.

pending_qa.q: How does a coach's lived experience and personal background shape their unique framework?
pending_qa.r: A coach's lived experience is the very thing that sets their process apart from somebody else's. Nobody has the exact unique combination of life experience that formulates how a coach makes decisions, teaches, and delivers information. While many coaches may talk about similar ideas, those ideas are filtered through each coach's own life experience, which makes their process distinctly theirs. This is why two coaches talking about frameworks will not do it the same way—the lived experience is what makes the framework proprietary to that individual coach.
